leads.name: Plane tree(s) of Sarphatipark
leads.species: London Plane (Platanus x acerifolia), possibly other species (weeping willow, Austrian oak, silver maple, bald cypress and dawn redwood are all documented in the park)
leads.why_not_shipped: Park opened 1885, so any original planting is only ~140 years old; monumentaltrees.com lists it as a monumental plane tree in its Amsterdam database but the page returned HTTP 403 on every fetch attempt so the specific girth/age/exact-tree location could not be pulled, and no second independent source with a specific remarkable claim (not just 'a plane tree in a park') was found in this pass. About 700m from the published ams_010 Rijksmuseum Wingnut, so genuinely inside the existing walkable cluster if a specific standout specimen can ever be confirmed. Worth a retry with a working monumentaltrees fetch or a direct approach to the municipality's Sarphatipark page (also 403'd here).

leads.name: Amsterdam's own 'bijzondere bomen' (special trees) municipal register, Centrum district
leads.species: n/a - a register, not a tree
leads.location_hint: maps.amsterdam.nl/bomen_bijzonder/, Centrum district list went to public consultation Feb-Mar 2025
leads.why_not_shipped: RESOLVED 2026-08-08: licence checked and confirmed usable (Gemeente Amsterdam Maps Data terms, https://maps.amsterdam.nl/open_geodata/terms.php, proving sentence: 'U mag de dataset zowel voor niet-commerciele als commerciele doeleinden gebruiken', both commercial and non-commercial reuse permitted, attribution not required). Full dataset (5,827 trees citywide, dataset id 561, KAARTLAAG=BOMEN_BIJZONDER) downloaded and saved to data/registers/amsterdam-bijzondere-bomen.json with a full licence block. Used this pass to source ams_012 through ams_017. Not yet exploited outside the Plantage/Hortus/Artis area; a future pass should mine it for other Amsterdam clusters (Sarphatipark, Vondelpark, Oosterpark, Frankendael, canal-ring courtyards all have entries in it, see notes below).

leads.name: Begijnhof inner garden trees
leads.species: unknown - historically linden (leilindes) planted near the garden house image of the Virgin Mary
leads.location_hint: Begijnhof, Amsterdam-Centrum, approx. 52.3678, 4.8899 (about 0.8 km from the published cluster)
leads.why_not_shipped: CHECKED AGAINST THE REGISTER 2026-08-08: nothing within 250m of the Begijnhof courtyard qualifies. The register shows a dense run of city-owned elms (mostly Huntingdon-iep and Hollandse iep, planted 1920-1990, largest girth 274cm) that reads as ordinary canal-side street planting, not a designated remarkable specimen, plus one private 1925 walnut and a few private planes/maples in the 200-260m range, none flagged with any distinguishing note. Downgrading this lead: a text search and a register check have both come up empty. Only worth reopening with a site-visit-style photo source (iNaturalist, Flickr) if someone specifically wants to confirm the courtyard's own historic linden by observation rather than record.

leads.name: Park Frankendael monumental trees (beech, oak, ash, poplar, maple)
leads.species: European Beech, Pedunculate Oak, Ash, Poplar, Field Maple (mixed, per monumentaltrees.com's count of 6 described trees in the park)
leads.why_not_shipped: Roughly 3-4 km from the existing published cluster, too far to join it, and would need to stand as its own second cluster. Not pursued this pass because time ran out before any individual tree in the park could be identified and verified against two sources; the monumentaltrees.com park page also returned 403. CHECKED AGAINST THE REGISTER 2026-08-08: within 500m of the park there is a run of 12+ 'Zwarte Linde' (black lime, Tilia europaea 'Zwarte Linde') all planted 1870, girths 150-242cm, reading as a formal avenue/allee rather than individual specimens (an ensemble, not obviously a single collectible point per the hard rule); plus a single Gewone Plataan (London Plane) from 1845, girth 609cm, about 1.2km away and owned by the Gemeente, which is a much stronger single-specimen candidate and the oldest Gemeente-owned tree found in this whole pass outside Artis. Worth a dedicated pass: verify that 1845 plane (register_id 456444, 52.3603135,4.9248302) plus whatever individual specimens the park's own beech/oak/ash/poplar/maple set turns out to be, now that the register gives exact coordinates to start from instead of a blind park search.

leads.name: Sarphatipark plane tree(s)
leads.species: London Plane (Platanus x acerifolia/hispanica) and other park species
leads.why_not_shipped: CHECKED AGAINST THE REGISTER 2026-08-08: nothing in the Gemeente's bijzondere bomen register falls inside Sarphatipark itself; the nearest registered entries are 1+ km away in Vondelpark/Weteringplantsoen direction. Either the park genuinely has no municipally-designated special tree, or (per the register's own 'groeikaart, wordt gebiedsgewijs geactualiseerd' caveat) De Pijp/Oud-Zuid simply has not been surveyed yet. Combined with the still-unresolved monumentaltrees.com 403 from the previous pass, downgrading this lead: two independent lookup attempts have both failed to produce a specific standout specimen.

leads.name: Existing ams_011 (Turkish Hazel of the Hortus) has an exact tree-level coordinate now available
leads.why_not_shipped: NOT A NEW CANDIDATE, an upgrade opportunity for an already-published tree, noted here rather than silently edited (this pass does not edit city files). ams_011 is currently location_precision: approximate, pinned at the Hortus street address. The newly-imported municipal register carries the same tree (matched on distinctive species, 1795 planting date and the Bomenstichting source id 1686149 that ams_011's own notes already cite) at an exact surveyed point, 52.3670831,4.9090584, about 70m from the current approximate pin. A future pass or the merging session could upgrade ams_011's coordinates and flip location_precision to confirmed on this basis.
